meta.audience: The multitude, and then the twelve directly
meta.location: The temple in the land Bountiful
meta.unit: The sermon at the temple (3 Nephi 12–14)
principles: Reward paid by the one who sees in secret
A prayer given without two of its petitions
An instruction narrowed to twelve men

world_behind.title: Alms are commanded before they are qualified
world_behind.text: Verse 1 opens with a positive instruction to do alms unto the poor. Matthew 6:1 begins with the warning and never gives the command, so the Nephite version establishes the duty before regulating it.

world_behind.title: The triad follows Matthew 6 in order
world_behind.text: Alms, prayer, and fasting each receive a hypocrite's version, a secret version, and the same promise of open reward, in the same sequence as Matthew 6:1 through 18. The structure carries over whole, and every difference sits inside it.

world_behind.title: The prayer is shorter here
world_behind.text: Verses 9 through 13 omit "Thy kingdom come" and "Give us this day our daily bread," both present in Matthew 6:10 and 11. Of everything this chapter alters in Matthew, these two omissions are the largest.

world_behind.title: The closing praise is present
world_behind.text: Verse 13 keeps "For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever," which Matthew 6:13 also carries and which many later manuscripts of Matthew do not.

world_behind.title: The fasting instruction is carried over
world_behind.text: Verses 16 through 18 keep the anointed head and the washed face of Matthew 6:17, in the same chapter where the prayer has lost two petitions. What was kept is as much an editorial fact as what was dropped.

world_behind.title: Mormon marks the audience change in his own text
world_behind.text: Verse 25 breaks the discourse to report that Jesus looked upon the twelve whom he had chosen and spoke to them, before continuing with the words of Matthew 6:25. Matthew has no such break, and the insertion narrows a public sermon onto its leadership at that exact line.

world_behind.title: The Gentile clause is dropped
world_behind.text: Verse 32 omits "for after all these things do the Gentiles seek," which stands in Matthew 6:32. The audience is a remnant of Israel on the far side of the world, and the comparison had nobody to point at.

words.text: Gifts to the poor. All five of the record's uses are in this chapter, at verses 1 through 4, and the King James Bible has it thirteen times, mostly in Acts.
Made holy, treated as holy. The record uses the word twice, here and at Mosiah 13:19 of the sabbath, and the King James Bible twenty-two times.
To spoil the appearance of. It appears once in the record, and once in the King James Bible, at Matthew 6:16, in this same saying about fasting.
Wealth, personified as a rival master. The word occurs once in the record and four times in the King James Bible, and is left untranslated in both.
A unit of length, about the forearm. The word turns up once here, and forty-five times in the King James Bible, where it is nearly always a building measure. Here it measures a man's height.
Wild flowers. One use here against ten in the King James Bible. Verse 28 sets them against Solomon's wardrobe.

phrases.term: I would that ye should do alms unto the poor
phrases.text: The positive command that Matthew 6:1 lacks. The warning about being seen follows it rather than standing alone.

phrases.term: Let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth
phrases.text: Secrecy pressed past other people to yourself. The giving is to be hidden from the giver's own accounting.

phrases.term: Enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door
phrases.text: Two actions, and not one. Alma 33:7 has a prayer offered in a closet as well.

phrases.term: Use not vain repetitions, as the heathen
phrases.text: The reason follows: they think they will be heard for much speaking. 3 Nephi 19:24 will describe disciples who did not multiply many words.

phrases.term: Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name
phrases.text: The prayer's opening, identical to Matthew 6:9. What comes next is where the two diverge.

phrases.term: They disfigure their faces that they may appear unto men to fast
phrases.text: The performance described physically. Verses 17 and 18 give the opposite instruction in equally physical terms.

phrases.term: Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also
phrases.text: The direction of the claim. The heart follows the treasure, so the treasure is the thing to place.

phrases.term: If thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light
phrases.text: The eye as the body's lamp. Verse 23 pushes it further: light that has become darkness is a greater darkness.

phrases.term: Ye cannot serve God and Mammon
phrases.text: The end of the section on treasure. The impossibility is stated flatly rather than argued.

phrases.term: He looked upon the twelve whom he had chosen, and said unto them
phrases.text: Mormon marking a change of audience. What follows in Matthew 6:25 is general, and here it is given to twelve men with a ministry.

phrases.term: Seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness
phrases.text: The instruction the whole section arrives at. Jacob 2:18 had put the same order in the same words.

verses.label: v. 1–34
verses.title: Where the changes fall
verses.text: Eighteen of this chapter's thirty-four verses carry a real word change against the King James text, fifty-three per cent, which puts it thirteenth among the twenty-four chapter-length quotations in the volume. The count overstates the disturbance. Seven of the twenty-four substitutions are the single swap which to who in a relative clause referring to a person, and several more are spelling regularised. Set those aside and the chapter's real work is done in five places: verse 1, the prayer, verse 25, verse 30 and verse 32.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: A command in front of the warning
verses.text: The King James chapter opens on a prohibition: "Take heed that ye do not your alms before men." Sixteen words are set in front of it here, "Verily, verily, I say that I would that ye should do alms unto the poor; but take heed." The prohibition is untouched and now arrives as the second half of a sentence whose first half commands the thing being regulated. Matthew's opening tells a hearer how not to give; this one tells him to give, and then how not to.

verses.label: v. 9–12
verses.title: Two petitions missing
verses.text: The Lord's Prayer here is two lines shorter than the King James version. "Thy kingdom come" is gone from verse 10, and "Give us this day our daily bread" is gone from what would be verse 11. Because the text is set out in the same verse count, everything after shifts up one: the King James verse 12, forgiveness of debts, stands at verse 11 here, and the King James verse 13 stands at verse 12. Of the six petitions Matthew records, four remain, and the two removed are the only two that ask for something to arrive, a kingdom and a meal.

verses.label: v. 13
verses.title: The ending that manuscripts argue about
verses.text: The prayer closes here on a line of praise, "For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amen." Those words are printed in the King James Bible and are missing from the oldest surviving Greek manuscripts of Matthew, where the prayer ends at deliverance from evil. This is worth setting beside 3 Nephi 12:22, which goes the other way: there the chapter omits "without a cause," a phrase the King James prints and the oldest Greek manuscripts also lack. Within one sermon, one passage follows the older reading and another follows the later one.

verses.label: v. 25
verses.title: Who is being told not to worry
verses.text: In Matthew the instruction to take no thought for food and clothing runs on from the saying about two masters, addressed to everyone listening. Here forty-four words are inserted first: "when Jesus had spoken these words he looked upon the twelve whom he had chosen, and said unto them: Remember the words which I have spoken. For behold, ye are they whom I have chosen to minister unto this people." Only then does "Therefore I say unto you, take no thought for your life" begin. The audience for the rest of the chapter is twelve men with a job, not a crowd.

verses.label: v. 30
verses.title: A question turned into a condition
verses.text: Matthew ends the argument from the lilies with a rebuke shaped as a question: "shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?" Here the question mark is gone and the sentence makes a bargain instead, "even so will he clothe you, if ye are not of little faith." Nothing about the grass or the oven changes. What changes is that the hearers are no longer being told off for a faith they already lack; they are being told what follows if they have it.

verses.label: v. 32
verses.title: The Gentiles left out
verses.text: The King James verse begins with a parenthesis, "(For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:)", and this version deletes it, leaving "For your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things." The comparison that motivated the warning is gone, and with it the only place the word Gentiles stands in Matthew 5 through 7. The three chapters of the sermon as given here do not use it at all. What remains is the reassurance without the contrast that set it up.

chapter.title: The chapter opens with a command to give
chapter.text: Verse 1 puts the alms before the warning. The instruction is not only about how to avoid a fault.

chapter.title: The same structure runs three times
chapter.text: Hypocrite, secret, open reward. Alms, prayer, and fasting are treated as one lesson in three forms.

chapter.title: Two petitions are absent from the prayer
chapter.text: No kingdom come, no daily bread. The record gives the prayer as spoken here and does not comment on the difference.

chapter.title: The closing praise is kept
chapter.text: Verse 13 ends with the kingdom, the power, and the glory. The record gives the prayer as it was spoken here.

chapter.title: Forgiveness is made reciprocal in two verses
chapter.text: Verses 14 and 15 state it positively and then negatively. Nothing else in the prayer gets that treatment.

chapter.title: The audience narrows and it is marked
chapter.text: Verse 25 has Mormon reporting the look at the twelve. The instruction about taking no thought is addressed to men who are being sent out.

chapter.title: The clothing promise carries a condition
chapter.text: Verse 30 makes it depend on not being of little faith, where Matthew 6:30 puts the phrase as a question to the hearers.

chapter.title: The section ends on order rather than on unconcern
chapter.text: Verse 33 says seek first. The instruction is about sequence and not about indifference to needs.

applications.title: Hide it from yourself too
applications.text: The left hand is not to know. Not only concealment from an audience but from your own bookkeeping; a good deed you are still counting is not yet finished.

applications.title: Shut the door
applications.text: Two actions are named: go in, and close it. A place and a barrier, both physical. If your prayer keeps getting interrupted, the instruction here is about furniture before it is about attitude.

applications.title: Say the pattern, not the words
applications.text: The prayer is introduced as a manner, "after this manner therefore pray ye," and what follows is short enough to memorise and general enough to fill in. Learn the shape, and use it as a checklist for what your own praying leaves out.

applications.title: Attach the condition you would rather not
applications.text: The forgiveness clause is the only line of the prayer given a follow-up, and it is stated twice, once positively and once negatively. Whatever else you ask for this week, notice that this one comes with your own conduct written into it.

applications.title: Place the treasure and let the heart follow
applications.text: The verse runs from treasure to heart, not the other way. If you want to care about something, put something of yours into it and wait.

applications.title: Pick which master before the day starts
applications.text: The verse rules out neutrality: hate one and love the other, or hold to one and despise the other. There is no third arrangement offered. Decide the order in advance, because the moment of collision is a poor time to work it out.

applications.title: Notice when instruction is addressed to a role
applications.text: Taking no thought for food and raiment is said to the twelve, who have just been given a full-time errand. Before applying a sentence to yourself, check who was standing in front of the speaker.

applications.title: Sort the two questions
applications.text: Seek the kingdom first, and take no thought for tomorrow. One is about priority and one is about horizon, and the verse joins them. When you are anxious, ask which of the two is actually wrong: the ranking, or the distance you are looking.

questions.text: Whom have I given to lately, and who knows about it?
Where do I actually pray, and is there a door?
What in my praying is repetition I am counting on?
If someone tracked my spending, what would they say I love?
Which two masters am I currently trying to serve?
What am I seeking first, honestly?

entries.reason: the calling of those twelve, counted in a parenthesis

targets.quote: the number of them who had been called, and received power and authority to baptize, was twelve)
targets.verse_text: And it came to pass that when Jesus had spoken these words unto Nephi, and to those who had been called, (now the number of them who had been called, and received power and authority to baptize, was twelve) and behold, he stretched forth his hand unto the multitude, and cried unto them, saying: Blessed are ye if ye shall give heed unto the words of these twelve whom I have chosen from among you to minister unto you, and to be your servants; and unto them I have given power that they may baptize you with water; and after that ye are baptized with water, behold, I will baptize you with fire and with the Holy Ghost; therefore blessed are ye if ye shall believe in me and be baptized, after that ye have seen me and know that I am.

targets.markdown: And now, for the sake of these things which I have spoken unto you—that is, for the sake of retaining a remission of your sins from day to day, that ye may walk guiltless before **God—I would that ye should impart of your substance to the poor**, every man according to that which he hath, such as feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, visiting the sick and administering to their relief, both spiritually and temporally, according to their wants.
